card.title: iPhone 16 Pro no power shorted VDD Main traced to CP3200B1G0 IC

source.title: I Think I Found the iPhone 16 Pro's Next Common Failure (And How To Fix It) — VCC Board Repairs - Jesse Cruz

claims.statement: A shorted CP3200B1G0 charging IC can pull VDD Main directly to ground on iPhone 16 series, causing a total no-power and no-charging fault.
claims.evidence: Applying 4.2V to the battery connector pulled 2.4-2.5A immediately; removing CP3200B1G0 cleared the short.
claims.quote: our fault was no power caused by a main short that happens to be on the charging IC... CP3200B1G0... all the 16 models will use this charging IC

claims.statement: A Mechanic USB-C pin tester showing 0.07 diode mode readings instead of OL on outer pins indicates a charging circuit short on the iPhone 16 Pro.
claims.evidence: The faulty board showed 0.07 on outer pins while the known good donor board read OL.
claims.quote: 0.07 is basically a short on the mechanic reader, and on the known good, it actually shows OL. So, we've already detected a fault right away.

claims.statement: SN2012027 is a charging controller IC situated near the CP3200B1G0 charging IC under the board shield.
claims.evidence: The technician damaged and subsequently replaced the SN2012027 IC adjacent to CP3200B1G0.
claims.quote: The part number of this chip is SN2012027 and then on the bottom right 833.

procedure: Test charging port pins using a USB-C breakout/tester in diode mode to check for abnormal low readings vs known-good OL.
Connect a DC power supply set to 4.2V directly to the battery connector to test for immediate current draw before prompt to boot.
Use a thermal camera while feeding 4.2V to identify shorted components or hot spots on the board.
Carefully remove or cut the metal shield covering the charging circuit area using wire cutters.
Apply flux and use hot air set to 380°C and 50% airflow to remove the shorted CP3200B1G0 IC.
Prep pads with 183°C leaded solder and wick them flat.
Align a new CP3200B1G0 IC to the orientation mark on the board and solder it with hot air.
Re-test power supply draw to ensure the VDD Main short is resolved before full reassembly.

measurements.context: Immediate current draw at 4.2V before prompt to boot indicating short on VDD Main
Diode mode reading indicating short circuit on outer pins

measurements.point: Mechanic USB-C tester outer pins (known good)
measurements.context: Diode mode reading on working board

cautions: SOURCE RISK: Cutting or prying off shields with wire cutters can easily crush or chip adjacent micro-ICs such as the SN2012027 controller.
Applying excessive heat on double-layered sandwich boards risks separating interposer solder joints.
card.caveats: A VDD Main short can be caused by any connected component or capacitor; replacing CP3200B1G0 only resolves the fault if thermal imaging or diode readings isolate the short to that specific IC.
